mainTopic: תנאי כפול in the פסוקים of סוטה and sprinkling; the משנה on mistaken or future קידושין; and רבי יוחנן's rule that what is in a person's power counts as done.
overview: The גמרא first explains the strange phrase 'you shall eat the sword' (ישעיהו 1:20). רבא says it means harsh, unhealthy food. Next it tests the סוטה פסוק against the two opinions about תנאי כפול. רבי תנחום shows that the short spelling of הנקי also hints at חנקי, which gives רבי מאיר his second side. It also teaches רבי חנינא בן גמליאל that the punishment is severe. The גמרא then looks at the פסוקים about sprinkling for purity from a dead body and shows that each repeated phrase teaches its own law. A new משנה follows. A man's wrong assumption about a woman's family or wealth does not cancel קידושין. קידושין set to begin 'after' a change he cannot make happen now do not work, and an unborn girl can be betrothed only once the pregnancy is noticeable. In the גמרא, רבי יוחנן rules that anything in a person's power counts as already done. רב אסי challenges this from the convert case, and the גמרא answers that converting is not fully in the man's power. The reason, a teaching of רבי יוחנן, comes on the next amud.

steps.title: How can someone eat a sword?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the פסוק means by 'you shall eat the sword.'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'You shall eat the sword'? What does that mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask about a strange phrase in the פסוק it just discussed: 'חרב תאכלו,' 'you will eat the sword.' This sets up רבא's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase comes from the second half of the condition in ישעיהו 1:20, 'if you refuse and rebel, you will eat the sword.' Read plainly, eating a sword makes no sense, so the גמרא asks how to understand it.

keyTerms.meaning: You will eat, or be eaten (by)

phrases.english: "You shall eat the sword"?
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 1:20. The גמרא is asking how a person could 'eat' a sword.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֶרֶב תְּאֻכְּלוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up a phrase from the ישעיהו פסוק discussed just before this section.

steps.title: רבא: harsh foods that hurt like a sword
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that 'sword' means rough foods: coarse salt, hard barley bread, and onions.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: it means coarse salt, hard barley bread, and onions.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers that the 'sword' is a picture for poor, harsh food that damages the body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The punishment is not being stabbed. It is a poor diet of rough foods. These foods harm the body the way a sword would.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Coarse grains of salt,
hard barley bread, and onions.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'sword' means harsh foods that harm the body.

steps.title: Support: these foods harm the body like swords
steps.stepSummary: A teaching of 'מר' backs up רבא: dry bread with salt and onions is as harmful as swords.
steps.simpleTranslation: As מר said: dry bakery bread with salt, and onions, are as hard on the body as swords.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an earlier teaching that supports רבא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's reading could seem like a stretch, so the גמרא shows that a known saying already compares these exact foods to swords. That saying is what links the word 'sword' to food.

keyTerms.meaning: Bread baked in a bakery oven

phrases.english: As the Master said:
Dry bakery bread with salt, and onions,
are harmful to the body like swords.
phrases.notes: Notice the wordplay: חֲרֵיבָה (dry) sounds like חֲרָבוֹת (swords).

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's answer.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's reading of 'sword' as harsh food
steps.raayaSupportSource: A known teaching of 'מר' comparing these foods to swords

steps.title: The סוטה verse seems to leave out רבי מאיר's second half
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק of סוטה states only the 'innocent' side. That fits רבי חנינא בן גמליאל, but רבי מאיר needs the guilty side too.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works for רבי חנינא בן גמליאל, since the פסוק says 'If no man lay with you… be free.' But for רבי מאיר, it should also say '[if he did,] be choked'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now tests the two opinions on a new פסוק and challenges רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that a condition only works if both sides are spelled out (תנאי כפול). The סוטה פסוק here only says what happens if she is innocent ('you shall be free'). So by רבי מאיר it should also say what happens if she is guilty, namely 'חנקי.'

keyTerms.meaning: Granted; it works well for one side

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up הִנָּקִי (be free) with חִנְקִי (be choked). They differ by only one letter, ה versus ח, and the whole next step depends on that.

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Ḥanina ben Gamliel,
this is why it is written:
"If no man has lain with you,
and if you have not strayed into impurity
while under your husband, be free,"
but according to Rabbi Meir,
it should have said "be choked"!
phrases.notes: He means the פסוק should also say: and if a man did lie with you, you will be choked.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from ישעיהו to a new test case in the Torah.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's rule of תנאי כפול
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סוטה condition states only one side, so by רבי מאיר it should not work.

steps.title: רבי תנחום: the spelling hints at 'choked'
steps.stepSummary: The word הנקי is spelled in a way that can also be read as חנקי, so both sides are there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי תנחום said: it is written 'הנקי,' a spelling that also hints at 'חנקי.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי תנחום defends רבי מאיר. He says the guilty side is hidden in the spelling of the word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because of how הנקי is spelled, it can be read two ways: 'be free' and 'be choked.' So the פסוק does state both sides, and רבי מאיר's rule holds.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written (how the word is spelled)

phrases.english: Rabbi Tanḥum said:
"הנקי" is written.
phrases.notes: The word is spelled short, without a י, so you can read it as הִנָּקִי (be free) or as חִנְקִי (be choked).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the spelling to find a hidden second meaning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק states only the innocent side.
steps.terutzMaskana: The spelling also says 'חנקי,' so both sides are stated.

steps.title: Then why does רבי חנינא בן גמליאל need the hint?
steps.stepSummary: Now that the spelling hints at 'choked,' the גמרא asks what that hint teaches according to רבי חנינא בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works for רבי מאיר, which is why 'הנקי' is written. But according to רבי חנינא בן גמליאל, why is it needed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא flips the challenge. Now the extra hint seems unneeded for רבי חנינא בן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא בן גמליאל holds that a condition does not need both sides. So for him, the hidden 'חנקי' seems to serve no purpose.

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Meir,
this is why "הנקי" is written,
but according to Rabbi Ḥanina ben Gamliel,
why do I need it?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי תנחום's answer to challenge the other opinion.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both sides are not required, the hidden 'חנקי' seems extra.

steps.title: The hint teaches that the guilty side is punished severely
steps.stepSummary: Without the hint, we might think a guilty סוטה has only broken a plain prohibition. The hint teaches that she is 'choked.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed. You might have thought: if no man lay with you, be free; and if he did, neither free nor choked, just a plain prohibition. The hint teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רבי חנינא בן גמליאל needs the hint for a different reason: to teach what the punishment is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי חנינא בן גמליאל, the hint is not needed to make the condition work. It is needed to tell us the result: a guilty סוטה is 'choked,' not just guilty of a plain prohibition.
steps.whatToRemember: The same hidden 'חנקי' works for both opinions. For רבי מאיר it completes the doubled condition. For רבי חנינא בן גמליאל it teaches that the guilty side is severely punished.

phrases.english: It is necessary,
for it might enter your mind to say:
"If no man has lain" – be free,
"and if he has lain" – neither be free nor be choked,
but rather it is merely a prohibition,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִצְטְרִיךְ סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רבי חנינא בן גמליאל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The hint is given a different purpose (teaching the punishment)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A guilty סוטה has only broken a plain prohibition.
steps.terutzMaskana: She is 'choked,' meaning she receives the severe punishment.

steps.title: New challenge: the doubled verse about purification
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק about purifying from a dead body states both sides. That fits רבי מאיר, so why would רבי חנינא בן גמליאל need it?
steps.simpleTranslation: It works for רבי מאיר, since it says 'He shall purify himself on the third and seventh day and be pure; and if he does not purify himself…'. But according to רבי חנינא בן גמליאל, why is this needed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge against רבי חנינא בן גמליאל from another פסוק. This sets up an answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק spells out both sides, which matches רבי מאיר's rule of תנאי כפול. If both sides are not required, as רבי חנינא בן גמליאל holds, the second half looks extra.

keyTerms.meaning: He will purify himself (with the purifying water)
And so on (the rest of the פסוק)

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Meir,
this is why it is written:
"He shall purify himself with it on the third day
and on the seventh day, and he shall be pure;
but if he does not purify himself, etc."
but according to Rabbi Ḥanina ben Gamliel,
why do I need it?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב הוּא יִתְחַטָּא בוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new test case after the סוטה discussion is resolved.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק doubles the condition, which seems extra if doubling is not required.

steps.title: Both sprinkling days are required, not just one
steps.stepSummary: The 'both sides' wording of the פסוק teaches that sprinkling on only the third or only the seventh day does not work, even after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed. You might have thought: the מצוה is to sprinkle on the third and the seventh day, but if he did it on only one of them, it still counts. So the פסוק teaches us that it does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 8. Even for רבי חנינא בן גמליאל, the double wording of the פסוק still teaches something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the 'if not, he will not be pure' half, we could think the two days are only the ideal way, and one sprinkling is enough after the fact. The negative half shows that both sprinklings are a must. So רבי חנינא בן גמליאל does not need this פסוק as a source for תנאי כפול.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed; the words have a purpose
You might have thought (the mistaken first idea)
Sprinkling the purifying water on someone who became impure from a dead body

phrases.english: It is necessary, for it might enter your mind to say:
The מצוה of sprinkling is on the third and on the seventh day,
but where he did it on just one of them, he has done it.
phrases.notes: Meaning it would still count after the fact, even though doing both is the ideal.

phrases.english: So it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִצְטְרִיךְ, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: The extra words teach a separate law, so they are not needed for תנאי כפול
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Sprinkling on both days is only the ideal, and one day is enough after the fact
steps.terutzMaskana: Both sprinklings are required. Without both, he is not pure.

steps.title: Why does the Torah repeat the sprinkling days?
steps.stepSummary: A later פסוק repeats 'on the third day and on the seventh day.' Why is this repetition needed?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the pure one shall sprinkle on the impure one on the third day and on the seventh day.' Why do I need this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now looks at a second פסוק in the same פרק. It asks why the days are said again when we already know them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 showed that both days are required. So this new mention of the third and seventh days seems extra. The גמרא wants to know what new thing it teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? (asking about extra words)
The pure person (who does the sprinkling)
The impure person (who receives the sprinkling)

phrases.english: "And the pure shall sprinkle on the impure
on the third day and on the seventh day"
Why do I need it?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 9 explained one פסוק, the גמרא asks about another phrase that seems extra
steps.kashyaTarget: The repeated mention of the third and seventh days in במדבר 19:19
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The days were already stated earlier, so saying them again seems to teach nothing new

steps.title: The days are fixed, even if you add days in between
steps.stepSummary: Without this פסוק we might think only an early sprinkling is a problem, and a late one (third and eighth) is fine. The פסוק teaches that the days are exact.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed. You might have thought: 'third' is to rule out the second day, and 'seventh' is to rule out the sixth, because doing it early cuts down the days of purity. But if he sprinkled on the third and the eighth, adding to the days of purity, I might say that is fine. So the פסוק teaches us it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the repeated פסוק teaches that the sprinkling days are exact. Sprinkling later than the set day does not work either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might think the Torah only cares about not sprinkling too soon, since that shortens the waiting time. Sprinkling later only makes the wait longer, so it might seem fine. The repetition teaches that the days must be exactly the third and the seventh.

keyTerms.meaning: The days of purity; the waiting days of the purifying process
It is fine; it is acceptable

phrases.english: It is necessary, for it might enter your mind to say:
'Third' is to exclude the second day,
'seventh' is to exclude the sixth day,
because he would be lessening the days of purity,
phrases.notes: Sprinkling early would shorten the waiting time between the sprinklings.

phrases.english: but where he did it on the third and the eighth day,
where he is adding to the days of purity,
I might say it is fine.
So it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִצְטְרִיךְ, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: שְׁלִישִׁי לְמַעוֹטֵי שֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: The repetition teaches a new detail: the days are exact
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only sprinkling too early is a problem. Sprinkling later (third and eighth) is acceptable.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sprinklings must be on exactly the third and the seventh day. A later day does not work either.

steps.title: Why does the Torah add 'he shall purify him on the seventh day'?
steps.stepSummary: The same פסוק also says 'and he shall purify him on the seventh day.' Why is this phrase needed?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he shall purify him on the seventh day.' Why do I need this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about one more phrase in the same פסוק that also seems extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know that the seventh day is the second sprinkling day. So this phrase seems to add nothing, and the גמרא asks what it teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall purify him (complete his purification)

phrases.english: "And he shall purify him on the seventh day"
Why do I need it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחִטְּאוֹ בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another seemingly extra phrase in the same פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The seventh day was already mentioned, so this phrase looks extra

steps.title: Two sprinklings are needed even for תרומה
steps.stepSummary: Without this phrase we might think two sprinklings are needed only for קדשים, and one is enough for תרומה. The פסוק teaches that two are needed for both.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed. You might have thought: this rule is only for קדשים, but for תרומה one sprinkling is also enough. So the פסוק teaches us that it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the phrase teaches that two sprinklings are needed even to eat תרומה. This ends its look at the extra words in the sprinkling פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קדשים are holier than תרומה, so we might think the full process is needed only for them. The extra phrase shows that one sprinkling is not enough even for תרומה. So every repeated phrase in these פסוקים teaches its own law.

keyTerms.meaning: These words (this rule) apply only to...
The portion of produce given to a כהן, which must be eaten in purity

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי חנינא בן גמליאל, every 'extra' phrase in the פסוקים of sprinkling teaches its own law. Both days are a must, the days are exact, and both are needed even for תרומה. So these פסוקים do not show that a condition must be stated both ways.

phrases.english: It is necessary, for it might enter your mind to say:
This applies only to sacred offerings,
phrases.notes: "This" means the need for two sprinklings.

phrases.english: but for תרומה, even one is enough.
So it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִצְטְרִיךְ, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: הָנֵי מִילֵּי לְקׇדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: The phrase teaches a new detail: the rule covers תרומה too
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two sprinklings are needed only for קדשים. One is enough for תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two sprinklings are needed for תרומה as well.

steps.title: Mistaken about her family or wealth, she is still betrothed
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: if a man betroths a woman and later says he was wrong about her being from a כהן or לוי family, or about her being rich or poor, the קידושין still work, because she did not trick him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a man betroths a woman and says: 'I thought she was a כהן's daughter, but she is a לוי's daughter,' or 'a לוי's daughter, but she is a כהן's daughter,' or 'poor, but she is rich,' or 'rich, but she is poor,' she is betrothed, because she did not mislead him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that a man's own wrong assumption about a woman does not cancel the קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man made no condition, and the woman told him nothing false. The mistake came only from his own assumption, so the קידושין stand.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (a new משנה begins here)

steps.confusionAlert: The man was still mistaken here. The point is that she did nothing to cause his mistake, and he made no condition. That is why the קידושין stand.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who betroths a woman and says:
I thought that she was a priest's daughter,
and it turns out she is a Levite's daughter;
or a Levite's daughter, and she is a priest's daughter;
or poor, and she is rich;
or rich, and she is poor.
She is betrothed,
because she did not mislead him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַמְקַדֵּשׁ אֶת הָאִשָּׁה וְאָמַר: כְּסָבוּר הָיִיתִי שֶׁהִיא כֹּהֶנֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. The discussion of the פסוקים of sprinkling has ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man's own mistaken assumption about a woman's family or wealth does not cancel the קידושין when she did not mislead him.

steps.title: Betrothal that depends on a future change fails
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if a man says 'you are betrothed to me after I convert / after you convert / after I am freed / after you are freed / after your husband dies / after your sister dies / after your יבם does חליצה,' the woman is not betrothed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a man says to a woman, 'You are betrothed to me after I convert,' or 'after you convert,' or 'after I am freed,' or 'after you are freed,' or 'after your husband dies,' or 'after your sister dies,' or 'after your יבם does חליצה for you,' she is not betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a new case. It lists cases where a man tries to make קידושין that will only start in the future, after something changes, and rules that none of them work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In every case, right now the man cannot marry this woman at all, and the change that would allow it is not in his hands. So his words have nothing to take hold of, and the קידושין fail even after the change happens.

keyTerms.meaning: After I am freed (from being a slave)
Your יבם, the brother of your husband who died without children
Will do חליצה, the ceremony that releases a widow from her יבם

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not that the man is putting off the קידושין. The problem is that right now he has no ability to marry her, and the thing that would change this is not up to him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the idea, developed in the גמרא, that what matters is whether the thing is in the person's own power right now.

phrases.english: One who says to a woman:
'You are hereby betrothed to me
after I convert,' or 'after you convert,'
'after I am freed,' or 'after you are freed,'
'after your husband dies,' or 'after your sister dies,'
phrases.notes: The sister case means he is married to her sister, so he cannot marry her while his wife is alive.

phrases.english: 'after your יבם does חליצה for you'
she is not betrothed.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאוֹמֵר לָאִשָּׁה: ״הֲרֵי אַתְּ מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת לִי לְאַחַר שֶׁאֶתְגַּיֵּיר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new clause of the same משנה, after the clause about mistaken assumptions in קידושין (Step 14).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קידושין set to begin after a change the man cannot make happen now (conversion, freedom, death, חליצה) do not take effect.

steps.title: Betrothing an unborn daughter
steps.stepSummary: Saying 'if your wife gives birth to a girl, she is betrothed to me' does not work, unless the wife was already noticeably pregnant. Then his words stand, and if a girl is born, she is betrothed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Likewise, if a man says to his friend, 'If your wife gives birth to a girl, she is betrothed to me,' the girl is not betrothed. But if the friend's wife was already pregnant and her pregnancy could be seen, his words stand, and if she gives birth to a girl, the girl is betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a related case about betrothing a baby girl who has not been born yet. It draws a line between a pregnancy that is already known and one that is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there is no known pregnancy, the girl does not exist in any real way yet, so the קידושין fail, just like the cases in the first half. Once the pregnancy can be seen, the baby already counts as something that exists, so the קידושין work if a girl is born.

keyTerms.meaning: Her pregnancy was noticeable (you could tell she was pregnant)

steps.confusionAlert: The man is speaking to the girl's father, because a father accepts קידושין for his young daughter. The new point is only about whether the unborn girl counts as existing yet.
steps.whatToRemember: קידושין cannot work on something that does not yet exist. An unborn baby counts as existing once the pregnancy is noticeable.

phrases.english: And likewise, one who says to his friend:
'If your wife gives birth to a girl,
she is hereby betrothed to me'
she is not betrothed.
If his friend's wife was pregnant
and her pregnancy was noticeable,
his words stand,
and if she gives birth to a girl, she is betrothed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן הָאוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵירוֹ: ״אִם יָלְדָה אִשְׁתְּךָ נְקֵבָה הֲרֵי זוֹ מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת לִי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a parallel case to the same משנה, with an exception for a known pregnancy.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Betrothing an unborn girl fails unless the pregnancy is already noticeable. Then, if a girl is born, she is betrothed.

steps.title: No תרומה from detached produce for attached produce
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה elsewhere: one may not separate תרומה from produce already picked for produce still growing in the ground, and if he does, it is not תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה there: One may not separate תרומה from picked produce for produce still attached to the ground. And if he did, his תרומה is not תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and brings a related rule from the laws of תרומה. It is setting up a question that will connect back to our משנה about things that will only happen later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Produce still growing in the ground does not yet need תרומה, so it cannot be covered by the picked produce. This matches the idea of our משנה: an act cannot take hold of something that is not ready for it yet.

keyTerms.meaning: Separating תרומה, the portion of produce given to a כהן
Detached: produce already picked from the ground
Attached: produce still growing in the ground

phrases.english: גמרא: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מסכת תרומות (1:5).

phrases.english: One may not separate תרומה from detached produce
for attached produce.
And if he separated it,
his תרומה is not תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם: אֵין תּוֹרְמִין מִן הַתָּלוּשׁ עַל הַמְחוּבָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by bringing a parallel rule from תרומה that will serve as the base for the next question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תרומה separated from picked produce for produce still in the ground does not take effect.

steps.title: What if the תרומה is set to take effect once the produce is picked
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי asks רבי יוחנן: what if someone says the picked produce should be תרומה for the growing produce, or the growing produce for the picked produce, 'when they are picked,' and then they are picked?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי asked רבי יוחנן: If someone said, 'The picked produce of this garden bed should be תרומה for the growing produce of this garden bed,' or 'The growing produce of this garden bed should be תרומה for the picked produce of this garden bed, when they are picked,' and then they were picked, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי asks a question that builds on the משנה just quoted. He wants to know whether delaying the תרומה until the produce is picked solves the problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said separating תרומה between picked and growing produce does not work. רב אסי asks about a person who makes it take effect only later, when everything will already be picked. This is just like the 'after' cases of our משנה, where קידושין set for the future failed.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (a question the asker did not know the answer to)

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב אַסִּי מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: רב אסי asked רבי יוחנן:
If he said, 'The picked produce of this garden bed
should be תרומה
for the growing produce of this garden bed,'
or, 'The growing produce of this garden bed

phrases.aramaic: יִהְיוּ תְּרוּמָה עַל פֵּירוֹת עֲרוּגָה זוֹ תְּלוּשִׁים
phrases.english: should be תרומה for the picked produce of this garden bed
when they are picked,' and they were picked, what is the law?
phrases.notes: 'When they are picked' is the new part. It goes on both statements, so nothing happens until the growing produce is picked.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב אַסִּי מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a version of the case in Step 17 where the תרומה is set to take effect only after picking.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does תרומה set to take effect 'when they are picked' work once the produce is actually picked?

steps.title: Anything in a person's power counts as already done
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that anything a person can do himself is not considered 'missing an action,' so the תרומה works.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Anything that is in a person's power to do is not considered as if it is missing an action.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers רב אסי's question. Since the owner can pick the produce any time he wants, the תרומה takes effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picking the produce is completely up to the owner, so the produce counts as if it were already picked. This is the difference from the cases in our משנה, like conversion, a husband's death, or a חליצה, which the man cannot make happen himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Anything that is in his hand (in his power to do)
Missing an action: something still has to be done before it is ready

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's rule: כל שבידו לאו כמחוסר מעשה דמי. If you can make it happen yourself, it counts as already done. That is why delayed תרומה works, while the 'after' cases of our משנה, which depend on things out of the man's control, do not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle explains the line in our משנה: future קידושין fail when the needed change is out of the man's hands.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Anything that is in his power
is not considered as lacking an action.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כֹּל שֶׁבְּיָדוֹ לָאו כִּמְחוּסָּר מַעֲשֶׂה דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אסי's question from Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תרומה takes effect, because picking the produce is in the owner's power, and something in a person's power is not considered 'missing an action.'

steps.title: רב אסי quotes the משנה about 'after I convert' as a challenge
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי brings the משנה that 'betrothed to me after I convert' (and similar cases) does not work, and sets it up as an objection to רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: He (רב אסי) objected to him (רבי יוחנן): The משנה says that if a man tells a woman, 'You are betrothed to me after I convert,' 'after you convert,' 'after I am freed,' 'after you are freed,' 'after your husband dies,' 'after your sister dies,' or 'after your יבם does חליצה for you,' she is not betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי quotes the same משנה we saw in step 15, but now he uses it as ammunition against רבי יוחנן. This step sets up the challenge; the actual point of the attack comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words of the משנה are being repeated for a new purpose. Before, it was just a ruling; now it is a test case for רבי יוחנן's rule that 'anything a person can do himself is not missing an action.' One of the cases on the list, 'after I convert,' looks like something the man can do himself.

keyTerms.meaning: After I am freed (from being a slave)

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
phrases.notes: This is רב אסי challenging רבי יוחנן's answer from the last step.

phrases.english: One who says to a woman:
"You are hereby betrothed to me
after I convert," "after you convert,"
"after I am freed," "after you are freed,"
"after your husband dies," "after your sister dies,"
"after your brother-in-law does חליצה for you" —
she is not betrothed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's answer in step 19 by bringing back the משנה from step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that anything a person can do himself is not considered 'missing an action.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה rules that 'betrothed after I convert' fails, even though converting seems to be in the man's own power. The full point is spelled out in the next step.

steps.title: Converting is in his own hands, so why doesn't it work?
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי explains his objection: most cases on the list are out of the man's control, but becoming a גר is something he can do himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that all the other cases are not in his power. But becoming a גר is in his power!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי spells out exactly what bothers him. Most cases in the משנה depend on things the man cannot control, but converting seems to be his own choice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband's death, a sister's death, or a יבם doing חליצה are not up to the man, so it fits that they fail. But he can decide to convert right now. By רבי יוחנן's rule, 'after I convert' should then work, yet the משנה says it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it makes sense (sets up 'but this one is a problem')
Not in his power / not up to him

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב אסי is bothered by all seven cases. He agrees that most of them fit רבי יוחנן's rule. His whole question is about the one case of converting.

phrases.english: Granted, all of them are not in his power,
but a convert — that is in his power!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא כּוּלְּהוּ לָאו בְּיָדוֹ, אֶלָּא גֵּר, הָוֵי בְּיָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the objection started in step 20 by pointing to the convert case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Converting is up to the man himself, so by רבי יוחנן it should not count as 'missing an action.' Yet the משנה says 'betrothed after I convert' fails.

steps.title: Converting is not really in his own hands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that becoming a גר is also not up to the man alone, and begins bringing a statement of רבי יוחנן to show why.
steps.simpleTranslation: Becoming a גר is also not in his power, as רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן by saying that converting is also not something the man can simply do on his own. It starts to bring a teaching of רבי יוחנן as the reason, and that teaching comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer does not change רבי יוחנן's rule. It changes how we see the convert case: becoming a גר is not just the man's own decision. So it is like the other cases on the list, and it fits that the קידושין fails.

phrases.english: A convert too is not in his power,
as Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:

steps.triggerLanguage: גֵּר נָמֵי לָאו בְּיָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אסי's objection from step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: converting is not actually in the man's own power.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב אסי assumed a man can become a גר whenever he chooses.
steps.terutzMaskana: Converting depends on more than his own choice. The reason is in רבי יוחנן's statement, which comes next. So it is like the other uncontrolled cases, and רבי יוחנן's rule stands.
